Rename or Add a Column

Source: R/utils.R
rename_or_add_column.Rd

Renames an existing column, or creates a new all-NA column when no old column name is supplied. Used throughout the WildObs mobilisation pipeline to coerce incoming spreadsheets into Camtrap DP column names.

Usage

rename_or_add_column(df, new_name, old_name)

Arguments

df

A data frame to modify.

new_name

Character string. The name the column should end up with. This is the second argument.

old_name

Character string. The existing column to rename. This is the third argument. If NA, "", or length zero, a new all-NA column is created instead of renaming.

Value

A data frame with the column renamed or added. The number of rows is always unchanged.

Details

The argument order is df, new_name, old_name — the new name comes before the old name. Some collaborator markdowns define their own inline copy of this helper using the opposite order. Those local copies shadow this one and are unaffected, but if you delete a local copy in favour of the package version, check the order at every call site before assuming it still works.

The function branches on old_name:

  1. If old_name is NA, an empty string, or length zero, a new column named new_name is appended and filled with NA.

  2. Otherwise the column currently named old_name is renamed to new_name.

  3. If no column matches old_name, the data frame is returned unchanged.

No collision check is performed. If new_name already names a different column, renaming leaves two columns sharing that name.

Author

Zachary Amir

Examples

df <- data.frame(lat = c(-27.5, -28.1), lon = c(153.0, 152.8))

# Rename an existing column: new name second, old name third
rename_or_add_column(df, "latitude", "lat")
#>   latitude   lon
#> 1    -27.5 153.0
#> 2    -28.1 152.8

# Passing "" as old_name adds a new all-NA column instead
rename_or_add_column(df, "coordinateUncertainty", "")
#>     lat   lon coordinateUncertainty
#> 1 -27.5 153.0                    NA
#> 2 -28.1 152.8                    NA

# An old_name that matches nothing returns the data frame untouched
rename_or_add_column(df, "latitude", "not_a_column")
#>     lat   lon
#> 1 -27.5 153.0
#> 2 -28.1 152.8
